title: Composer surface and toolcall fidelity lab notes
content:
Purpose:
Quick lab notes exploring a "composer" surface: a lightweight composition layer in the Hosted API that stitches multiple tool calls (internal and third-party), exposes progressive fidelity controls to clients, and provides predictable streaming semantics for partial structured output. This doc is exploratory — sketches, tradeoffs, and rough SDK ergonomics.

Top-level goals:
- Allow clients to declare a composition of toollets (a graph, linear list, or pipeline) and receive a single streaming response that includes partial structured frames as tool results complete.
- Provide fidelity knobs so client can trade off completeness vs latency (e.g., prefer partial summaries vs waiting for slow external tool).
- Keep server-side semantics simple: deterministic ordering where possible, idempotent tool calls, and well-defined retry semantics for partial frames.

Non-goals (for this lab):
- Full-blown workflow orchestration (we're not building a saga engine).
- Replacing Dedicated routing/placement decisions. This is API/SDK surface + light runtime routing hints only.

User stories (concrete):
1) Messaging app wants: summarize conversation with contact card lookups and a sentiment tool. They want early prefix summary while card lookups happen.
2) Support agent: needs immediate extractive highlights, then enriched answers once ticket DB search completes. Client wants a streaming envelope: "highlights" -> "answer-summary" -> "sources:list".
3) Marketplace app: compose a pricing tool (slow) + rules engine (fast); wants to spec partial correctness policy (best-effort pricing) for interactive UIs.

API sketch (high level):
POST /v1/composer/run
body: {
  "input": "user text",
  "composer": {
    "stages": [
      {"id": "extract", "tool": "extractor-v2"},
      {"id": "kb", "tool": "kb-search", "mode": "async"},
      {"id": "format", "tool": "formatter"}
    ],
    "fidelity": "progressive|conservative|speculative",
    "max_wait_ms": 1200
  }
}
Notes: keep simple typed enum fidelity. Clients can set max_wait_ms which indicates how long runtime should attempt to wait for slow tool results before emitting best-effort partial frames.

Streaming protocol concept:
- Use compact newline-delimited JSON frames (frame.type, frame.id, frame.payload) — compatible with existing incremental-output patterns but with explicit "stage_id" and fidelity metadata per frame.
- Frames: {"type":"partial","stage":"extract","fidelity":"progressive","payload":"..."} then later {"type":"commit","stage":"kb","payload":{"sources":[...]}}
- Guarantee: frames for a given stage are ordered; inter-stage ordering is best-effort (design choice: either enforce stage ordering or allow out-of-order commits with timestamps). For UX predictability enforce stage ordering at least for default-mode.

Toolcall idempotency and retries:
- All hosted-toollets must implement idempotent invoke semantics or be wrapped with at-least-once-safe proxies.
- For third-party integrations we surface a "retry_hint" and "partial_on_failure" policy in composer spec. Example: {"partial_on_failure": true, "fallback":"cached-stub"}

SDK ergonomics (JS/Go sketch):
- High-level client: compose({input, composer}).stream() -> EventEmitter of frames with typed events: 'stage.partial', 'stage.commit', 'status.update', 'error'.
- Convenience adapters for React-native: useComposerHook({ spec }) returns { frames, status, cancel } where frames array contains latest committed objects plus in-flight partials keyed by stage id.
- Client-side merge heuristics: simple default merging (last-commit wins), optional declarative merge hooks for apps that need custom reconciliation.

Structured output patterns:
- Adopt small canonical types: summary (text/html), table (rows/cols), list (items), sources (array of {id, weight, url}), actions (callable tool descriptors). Each frame announces schema version.
- Use typed validation in SDKs; default tolerant parsing with opt-in strict mode for enterprise customers.

Observability & debugging:
- Trace: every composer run gets a trace id. Frames include trace span for associated tool calls.
- Telemetry: counters for emitted partial frames, commits, partial_on_failure events, average time-to-first-frame, time-to-final-commit.
- Developer UX: provide a "replay" artifact — compact JSONL representing frame stream for a run (useful for offline debugging & reproducing flaky tool latency).

Operational constraints (runtime):
- Avoid head-of-line blocking: runtime should use per-stage time budgets and emit partials when budget exceeded.
- Batching implications: composing multiple toollets reduces batching opportunities for core token generation; recommend hints to runtime for co-batching compatible stages.
- Cost model: partials emitted despite downstream slow tools still incur their cost; expose fine-grained billing breakdown per-stage and per-frame in Console.

Open design tradeoffs (notes + opinions):
- Enforce strict stage ordering vs allow out-of-order commits: strict ordering is easier for client mental model but increases latency when some stages are slow; default strict with "allow_out_of_order": true as opt-in seems reasonable.
- Where to keep composition logic? API surface or client libraries? Keep canonical spec server-side but allow client-side composition helpers.
- Fallback policies: server-side canned fallbacks vs client-supplied stubs. Give customers both but default to safe canned stubs for security.

Risks and mitigations:
- Complexity creep: composer could turn into workflow engine. Mitigate by strictly scoping features (no persistent state, no long-running timers beyond a single request).
- Security: exposing tool call graphs could leak internal endpoints. Sanitize tool descriptors in public logs and provide allowlist per-tenant.
- Backcompat: adding new frame schemas — always include schema_version and graceful degrade path in SDKs.

Implementation roadmap (quick):
- Phase 0 (experiment): implement a prototype runtime adaptor that accepts a small composer spec and returns NDJSON frames. Target internal beta (SRE + Solutions Eng). (2 sprints)
- Phase 1: SDK surface + telemetry + Console breakdown. (3 sprints)
- Phase 2: Enterprise controls (strict fidelity policy, allowlists, replay storage). (2 sprints)

Open questions (for sync):
- Is schema_versioning per-frame adequate or do we need per-run manifest? (ask API infra)
- Billing semantics: charge per emitted token or per stage invocation? (finance ops input)

Next actions (short):
- Run small hackathon with Eng + SE to prototype composer NDJSON stream (owners: Avery, Samir).
- Create spike ticket ENG-1987 and link a very small demo in the Playground for product partners.
- Sync with Console team re: per-frame billing telemetry (Maya to own).

Notes to self / rough TODOs:
- Add small diagram of frame ordering (TODO: draw and add to Confluence).
- Draft example SDK pseudocode for TypeScript (include in next revision).

References/links: see linked_artifacts above; Slack thread #prod-hosted-composer -> thread ts 1678347234.

End of lab notes (very rough).
